translation_en: Narrated Sa'id bin Jubair: I said to Ibn 'Umar, 'A man accused his wife of adultery.' He replied, 'The Prophet (ﷺ) separated the two people of Banu 'Ajlan and said, "Allah knows that one of you is lying. Will either of you repent?" They both refused. He repeated, "Allah knows that one of you is lying. Will either of you repent?" They both refused, so he separated them.' Ayyub said: 'Amr bin Dinar told me something in the hadith that I do not see you narrating. He said that the man asked, "What about my property?" The Prophet said, "You have no claim to it. If you spoke the truth, you had intercourse with her; and if you lied, then it is even farther from you."'

Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the two who had invoked the curse: 'Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is lying, and you have no right to her.' The man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?' He replied, 'You have no claim to it. If you spoke truthfully about her, it was in return for what you made lawful of her; but if you lied about her, then it is even farther from you.'

Narrated Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'When a Muslim spends on his family seeking reward for it, that spending is charity for him.' This means that a person is rewarded for providing for his household when he does so seeking Allah's reward.
Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'Allah says: Spend, O son of Adam, and I will spend on you.' This is a promise that Allah will provide for the one who spends in His cause.

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'The one who strives to support a widow and a poor person is like one who fights in the way of Allah, or like one who prays throughout the night and fasts during the day.'

Narrated Sa'd: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to visit me when I was ill in Mecca. I said, 'I have wealth. May I bequeath all of it?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'Half?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'One third?' He said, 'One third, and one third is much. It is better to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them dependent, begging people with their hands. Whatever you spend is charity for you, even the morsel you place in your wife's mouth. Perhaps Allah will raise you in rank, and some people will benefit through you while others will be harmed by you.'

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'The best charity is what leaves a person self-sufficient, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand. Begin with those for whom you are responsible.' The wife says, 'Either you feed me or divorce me.' The slave says, 'Feed me and employ me.' The son says, 'Feed me; to whom will you leave me?' They asked Abu Huraira, 'Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' He said, 'No. This is from Abu Huraira's own store.'

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'The best charity is that given from what remains after one's needs are met, and begin with those for whom you are responsible.' That is, a person should first provide for the dependants whose care is his responsibility.

Muhammad bin Salam narrated to me: Waki' informed us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, who said: Ma'mar said to me that al-Thawri asked him, 'Have you heard anything about a man setting aside his family's provision for a year, or for part of a year?' Ma'mar said, 'I could not recall anything at the time.' Later I remembered a hadith that Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Malik bin Aws, from 'Umar: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to sell the date palms of Banu al-Nadir and reserve his family's provision for a year.'
